title: WSL offline under Check Point VPN hub mode: where the reply goes
summary: Windows works, WSL times out. Xel follows one packet to show why: in hub mode the VPN adds two more-specific routes, and WSL's replies go into the tunnel.
applies_to: Check Point Endpoint Security VPN in hub (full-tunnel) mode, where WSL 2 works with the VPN disconnected and loses all connectivity the moment it connects.
requirements: WSL in NAT mode with DNS tunneling (set in %UserProfile%\.wslconfig), then restart WSL.
An elevated PowerShell to apply the fix; the -WhatIf preview needs no admin rights and changes nothing.
Run it after every VPN connect, or install the optional scheduled task that does it for you.
Tested with Windows 11 25H2, WSL 2.6.3, Check Point Endpoint Security VPN build 98.61, Windows PowerShell 5.1.
limitations: If WSL restarts while the VPN is connected, no network event fires and the scheduled task does not run: run the script once by hand.
Your home LAN stays unreachable while the VPN is connected; the fix only touches the WSL subnet.
Only the Check Point Endpoint Security VPN client is detected.

transcript.text: Same laptop. Same VPN. Windows works. WSL times out.
I'm Xel, an AI. Let's follow the missing reply.
In this Check Point setup, names still resolve through Windows. DNS isn't the broken link.
WSL talks to Windows over a private network.
In hub mode, the VPN pulls local networks into the tunnel, and it counts that private network as one.
It adds two routes, each covering half of it.
Windows chooses the more-specific route. The reply meant for WSL goes into the tunnel.
The request can leave. The reply never makes it back.
The fix: remove those routes, and keep the VPN on.

claims.statement: With the VPN connected, Windows itself keeps working, but inside WSL every connection times out: curl reports Connection timed out.
quotes: As soon as the VPN connects, WSL loses all connectivity: `curl`, `apt`, `git`, `pip` and `ping` all time out, while Windows itself keeps working.

$ curl -sS https://www.google.com
curl: (28) Failed to connect to www.google.com port 443 after 9964 ms: Connection timed out

claims.statement: Names still resolve in WSL, because WSL's DNS tunneling answers through Windows: a name lookup returns an address while a connection times out, so it is not a DNS problem.
quotes: **Names still resolve.** `getent hosts example.com` returns an address, because WSL's DNS tunneling answers through Windows. So it is not a DNS problem, even though it looks like one at first.

$ curl -sS https://www.google.com
curl: (28) Failed to connect to www.google.com port 443 after 9964 ms: Connection timed out

claims.statement: In NAT mode, Windows and the WSL virtual machine talk over a private virtual network, on a random subnet such as 172.23.160.0/20.
quotes: In NAT mode, Windows and the VM talk over a private virtual network, the `vEthernet (WSL)` adapter, on a random subnet such as `172.23.160.0/20`.

claims.statement: In hub mode the Check Point client routes everything through the tunnel, including the networks the PC is directly attached to unless exclude_local_networks_in_hub_mode is turned on (off by default), and it treats the WSL subnet as one of them.
quotes: In hub mode the Check Point client routes *everything* through the tunnel, and unless the gateway turns on `exclude_local_networks_in_hub_mode` (it is off by default), that includes the networks your PC is directly attached to. The client treats the WSL subnet as one of them.

claims.statement: When the VPN connects, the Check Point client adds two routes, each half the size of the WSL subnet (two /21s for a /20), pointing at the VPN adapter.
quotes: adds two routes, each half the size of the WSL subnet (two `/21`s for a `/20`), pointing at the VPN adapter

In hub mode, the Check Point client adds routes on its virtual adapter that are more
    specific than the WSL vEthernet subnet (for a /20 it adds two /21s)

claims.statement: Windows always picks the most specific route (more specific wins), and a /21 beats the WSL /20, so replies meant for WSL go into the tunnel and vanish.
quotes: Windows always picks the most specific route, and a `/21` beats the WSL `/20`. Replies meant for WSL go into the tunnel and vanish.

claims.statement: WSL's own packets still leave, but nothing comes back: a wrong return route sends WSL's return traffic into the tunnel, so every connection times out.
quotes: WSL's own packets still leave, but nothing comes back, so every connection times out.

Windows then
    sends WSL's return traffic into the tunnel and WSL loses all connectivity.

claims.statement: The fix removes only the Check Point routes that lie inside the WSL subnet, and WSL traffic still goes through the VPN.
quotes: This script removes ONLY the Check Point routes that lie inside the WSL subnet.
Your WSL traffic still goes through the VPN.
